title: NFL insider hints at Vikings taking calls on J.J. McCarthy
description: Are the Minnesota Vikings already taking calls for J.J. McCarthy?
fullText:
Kyler Murray is officially the Minnesota Vikings' starting quarterback. The writing was on the wall when the signing was announced, and it has come true. Now that the dust has settled on the starting job, where does this leave J.J. McCarthy? According to one NFL analyst, Minnesota could already be fielding calls for the former Michigan Wolverine.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler said the front office has already been taking calls about McCarthy's availability, since he may not even be the full-time backup. Reports from Eagan, Minnesota, the site of Vikings training camp, say McCarthy could be battling for the QB2 job with Carson Wentz.

The timing of a potential McCarthy trade will indicate how the front office views Murray. If we see a trade take place before the season begins, or early in the season, the franchise clearly sees Murray as the future. In terms of package or teams, we could see a QB-needy team like the Jets, Browns, or Atlanta make a move to see if he can start right away.

Or, a team with an aging vet or even a lack of success with their current starter, like Philadelphia, Tampa, Detroit, or maybe the Chargers/Michigan reunion could take place.

title: Spurs Projected to Win Most NBA Games This Season
description: According to ESPN’s Insiders, the San Antonio Spurs are projected to win the most NBA games this coming season.The Spurs won 62 games this past season, which was the second-most in the NBA behind only the Oklahoma City Thunder, who won 64 games.Next year, the Spurs are projected to win 62 games again — two […] The post Spurs Projected to Win Most NBA Games This Season appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
According to ESPN's Insiders, the San Antonio Spurs are projected to win the most NBA games this coming season.

The Spurs won 62 games this past season, which was the second-most in the NBA behind only the Oklahoma City Thunder, who won 64 games.

Next year, the Spurs are projected to win 62 games again — two more than the Thunder, who are projected to win 60, according to ESPN.

Here are ESPN's Insiders' top-five projected teams in the NBA Western Conference as far as wins go for the 2026-27 season:

1. San Antonio Spurs (62-20)
2. Oklahoma City Thunder (60-22)
3. Denver Nuggets (51-31)
4. Houston Rockets (51-31)
5. Minnesota Timberwolves (50-32)

Given how good of a team that San Antonio is, it's not surprising to see them first in the Western Conference projections, especially since the team didn't lose any major parts like the Thunder, who lost several of their depth players like Lugentz Dort, Aaron Wiggins, and Isaiah Joe in trades due to the second apron.

The Spurs, meanwhile, added veteran Tobias Harris to a team that just went to the NBA Finals this past year, with perennial MVP candidate Victor Wembanyama leading the way for San Antonio.

As well, the team is expected to see Stephon Castle, Dylan Harper, and Carter Bryant take big leaps this coming season, plus you have valuable veterans such as De'Aaron Fox, Devin Vassell, Keldon Johnson, Julian Champagnie, and more propping up the team.

The team also added two first-round picks at the 2026 NBA Draft in Tarris Reed Jr. and Jayden Quaintance. With such a deep and talented team, you can see why ESPN's Insiders believe that the Spurs will be the top team in the league this season.

While the Spurs are expected to lead the Western Conference and the NBA overall, the defending champion New York Knicks are expected to lead the Eastern Conference, as the team is tied with the Detroit Pistons — who led the East with 60 wins last season — as the top team in the East this coming season.

1. New York Knicks (53-29)
2. Detroit Pistons (53-29)
3. Cleveland Cavaliers (51-31)
4. Philadelphia 76ers (50-32)
5. Boston Celtics (48-34)

The Knicks defeated the Spurs in the NBA Finals 4-1, so as good as San Antonio is, the Knicks were better last year, since they won it all when it mattered.

New York has a terrific team, though they did lose a valuable player in backup center Mitchell Robinson. He was replaced by veteran Andre Drummond, though it remains to be seen how that trade-off will look for the Knicks this coming season.

The Pistons were the top team in the East during the regular season last year, but they struggled a bit in the playoffs, and it will be interesting to see if they can keep up their winning ways next year or fall back to Earth.

The Philadelphia 76ers are projected for 50 wins, but if you ask most NBA fans, they probably would project them to win more than that after the team added NBA legend LeBron James in free agency.

title: ESPN predicts Warriors move up in Western Conference standings next season
description: ESPN predicts that the Golden State Warriors will finish the 2026-27 season with a 35-win campaign, two games worse than their total of 37 last year.
fullText:
The Golden State Warriors had an underwhelming 2025-26 season by many accounts, as injuries to both Jimmy Butler III and Stephen Curry never allowed them to find their footing in a loaded Western Conference playoff race. However, the Warriors were able to sneak into the NBA Play-In Tournament as the No. 10 seed, finishing with a 37-45 record.

Ahead of the 2026-27 season, ESPN recently predicted the records of all 30 teams, and their prediction for Golden State shouldn't come as a shock. ESPN expects the Warriors to finish with a 35-47 record, two wins worse than last year. However, ESPN does predict that a 35-win season will be good enough to move up in the Western Conference standings, passing the Los Angeles Clippers for ninth following the departure of Kawhi Leonard. If Golden State were to win fewer than last year's total of 37 games, it'd mark their worst campaign since the 2019-2020 season, where they finished with 15 victories.

title: Mike Vrabel reveals why he doesn't play Drake Maye in NFL Preseason
description: Drake Maye had a breakout "sophomore" NFL season. His head coach, Mike Vrabel, elaborated on the decision not to play Maye this preseason.
fullText:
In his first full season as an NFL starting quarterback, Drake Maye quickly proved himself as the New England Patriots' next franchise quarterback.

Maye finished his sophomore season with 4,394 passing yards, 31 passing touchdowns and a 77.1 QBR, finishing Top-4 in each category. Add 450 rushing yards and four more scores, Maye helped New England clinch its first AFC East title since the 2019-20 NFL season. 1,000 postseason scrimmage yards and seven touchdowns later, Maye put the Pats back in their first Super Bowl – also since 2019.

As is customary with established starters, Maye isn't playing in the preseason, sitting out both of New England's first two games. During a Monday appearance on Massachusetts-based radio station WEEI, head coach Mike Vrabel elaborated on his decision to not play Patriots starters.

"We are the front office," Vrabel said via ESPN's Mike Reiss. "We are all making the decisions. We're all included in this. It was about the young guys we have to develop. You can see that the players we kept out of the game, those are the guys. And we have to be able to find some guys behind them to be backups, to be the first guy in … those are the things that we are trying to develop and I guess that's what I was referencing."

Don't expect to see Maye during New England's preseason finale this coming Thursday, which will be an 8 p.m. kickoff at the 0-2 Cleveland Browns.

When the Patriots open their regular season with a Super Bowl rematch at the Seattle Seahawks, expect Maye to continue as a featured part of the reigning AFC East Champions' offense.

title: Jacob Lane evolving as a leader & pass rusher for Washington football
description: The Washington Huskies are looking to lean on Jacob Lane to anchor their pass rush on and off the field.
fullText:
The Washington Huskies have high hopes for outside linebacker Jacob Lane in the 2026 season.

The in-state product of Emerald Ridge High School in Puyallup led Jedd Fisch's team in both tackles for loss (8.5) and sacks (4) during his junior campaign in 2025, and is showing off a skill set that could help him improve on both those numbers. As NFL scouts have taken a close look at him during fall camp, the 6-foot-5, 260-pound Lane has looked like a reliable pass rusher for defensive coordinator Ryan Walters.

That showed up in a big way during Saturday's mock game, as the senior was everywhere. As the first-team defense mainly matched up with the second-team offense, it felt like Lane was in the backfield on seemingly every play.

He finished his day with a pair of sacks, a tackle for loss on freshman running back Ansu Sanoe, and a fumble recovery on a botched handoff from freshman quarterback Derek Zammit, as he generated the havoc Walters has preached and has developed into a leader on Washington's defense.

"Football knowledge-wise, I'd say I'm at the peak of my game right now," Lane said before fall camp began at Washington's local media day. "Just overall being a leader, being a guy in the locker room that people can go to, being more open, I feel like that's a big thing I've improved on over the last three years."

With a deep rotation on the edge, headlined by freshman Ramzak Fruean, who Fisch named the starter opposite Lane following the mock game, the senior looks like one of the biggest keys to success for Washington's pass rush as the Huskies look to improve on the 24 sacks it recorded in 2025, which placed the Huskies at No. 12 in the Big Ten.

title: Decision on significant 49ers position battle might wait until Week 1
description: There doesn't seem to be a leader in the RB2 position battle between Kaelon Black and Jordan James.
fullText:
The San Francisco 49ers' backup running back competition won't be decided anytime soon.

Jordan James returned to practice this week after missing time with a rib fracture, reinserting himself into a battle for the No. 2 job behind Christian McCaffrey that rookie Kaelon Black had been building on in his absence. Offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak made clear the rotation is far from settled.

"Really happy to see Jordan back out there," Kubiak said. "We've loved Jordan. We've been excited about him. It's just been unfortunate not having him on the field as much, but he looks good. He's in really good shape. I think seeing other young players get out there and have success makes him hungry."

James, a fifth-round pick in 2025 out of Oregon, had been penciled in as the frontrunner for the RB2 role for much of the offseason before the injury sidelined him. Black, whom San Francisco took in the third round (No. 90 overall) out of Indiana after he rushed for more than 1,000 yards in 2025, seized the opening. He turned heads in his preseason debut against the Chargers, with 33 yards on eight carries, and Kubiak was complimentary of his first NFL action.

"I loved how he ran," Kubiak said of Black. "He really brought kind of a spark to our offense. He's a guy who you don't have to block it perfect every time... His first time in NFL action, the moment wasn't big for him. He didn't blink."

The room's third piece, Isaac Guerendo, remains out after a shoulder injury, further underscoring the value of settling the pecking order behind McCaffrey. Kubiak also pointed to Black's growth as a receiver as the next step in his development, calling it "a big part of his development for sure."

Rather than name a clear-cut backup, Kubiak indicated the Niners will lean on a rotation into the regular season. "We'll go into the game saying, 'Hey, this guy's the next guy up after Christian.' We'll have a rotation going... those guys are going to keep competing all the way up until the first week."

title: Giants Give Positive Injury Update on WR Malik Nabers
description: The New York Giants gave a positive injury update on superstar wide receiver Malik Nabers. The post Giants Give Positive Injury Update on WR Malik Nabers appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Even with 1 massive story after another for the New York Giants this offseason — including hiring a new head coach and trading away a 1st-round pick — the biggest story of them all might still be the health of superstar wide receiver Malik Nabers.

The most encouraging sign for Nabers came on Monday, when head coach John Harbaugh told the assembled media, "It's reasonable to assume" Nabers will play in the season opener barring any setbacks with his surgically repaired knee.

Nabers had 109 receptions for 1,204 yards and 7 touchdowns in 15 games as a rookie in 2024 but tore his ACL just 4 games into the 2025 regular season.

The Giants host the Cowboys for a primetime Sunday Night Football game in Week 1.

"John Harbaugh isn't ready to make any blanket statements on Malik Nabers for Week 1. But he did say … he's trending towards being ready for the Cowboys," ESPN's Jordan Raanan wrote on his official X account.

That wasn't the only positive step Nabers took toward rejoining the team on Monday.

"Another step for Malik Nabers and the Giants: He shed the red jersey and took part in 7-on-7 & 11-on-11," The New York Post's Connor Hughes wrote on his official X account. "He wasn't full (worked in for reps), but a step in right direction. He made a nice grab diving back for the ball on an intermediate route/curl. The Giants were without pads today, so not full contact in that sense, but a "contact" day for Nabers. Again … Week 1 looks good."

While Nabers still doesn't have a timetable for when he might return, he dismissed a question from reporters on Friday about if and when he might be able to return to the player he was as a rookie — although not dismissed in the way you might think.

"I have extreme confidence in myself," Nabers said. "And I not gonna put myself in any spot where I'm not gonna be better than what I was before. So I don't see myself being what I was before, what y'all saw my rookie year. I felt like that was basic … I hold myself to a very high standard, and I feel like that high standard, you're going to see it sooner or later."

The 1st hint Nabers might be ready for the season opener came when he avoided starting the season on the Physically Unable to Perform (PUP) List and has been running routes at full speed in individual drills.

"Giants place three players on the PUP list in advance of veterans reporting for training camp next week … and Malik Nabers is not one of them," USA Today's Art Stapleton wrote on his official X account on July 23. "Neither is Cam Skattebo, so flip out if you'd like."

Bleacher Report's Alex Kay put Nabers at the top of his list of "dark horse candidates" to win NFL Offensive Player of the Year in 2026.

"Despite Nabers' bursting onto the scene with one of the best rookie seasons in recent memory — he caught 109 passes for 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns in 15 games — and establishing himself as one of the best receivers in the league, he only has the 19th best odds of winning Offensive Player of the Year this season," Kay wrote on July 8. "Nabers' impending return will be a massive boon for a Giants squad working to take a major step forward in 2026. The team went all-in on a regime change and roster improvements this offseason, most notably placing John Harbaugh at the head coaching reins and bolstering Jaxson Dart's protection with first-round guard Francis Mauigoa."

title: Buffalo Bills UFL Star Could be Top Trade Piece Ahead of Roster-Cutdown Deadline
description: A Bills player who was a star in the UFL could be one of the trade pieces Buffalo might deal this offseason. The post Buffalo Bills UFL Star Could be Top Trade Piece Ahead of Roster-Cutdown Deadline appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Buffalo Bills must finalize their roster by Aug. 30 at 6 p.m. ET, trimming it to 53 players. One major decision they face is at running back.

Most teams typically keep three running backs on their 53-man roster, and the Bills appear to have already solidified their choices: James Cook, Ty Johnson and Ray Davis. However, Frank Gore Jr. and Ian Wheeler are pushing hard to earn a roster spot.

If Wheeler does not make the 53-man roster, there is a possibility that the Bills will release him and attempt to re-sign him to the practice squad. But Wheeler would need to clear waivers for that to happen, which might be difficult given how well he has performed.

Buffalo should consider trading Wheeler, and Bills' SI Randy Gurzi named him as one of the possible top trade candidates on the roster.

"Undrafted rookie Ian Wheeler has been one of the standouts during the preseason. After recording 41 yards and a touchdown against the Panthers, Wheeler added 56 rushing yards and 21 receiving yards on Saturday against the Browns," Gurzi wrote on Monday. "It won't be easy for him to make the roster with James Cook, Ray Davis, and Ty Johnson all ahead of him, but his physical running style could make him popular among running back-needy teams. Rather than waiving him and risking getting nothing in return, the Bills could decide to add more draft capital, assuming they don't make the surprising move of keeping Wheeler over Johnson or Davis."

Wheeler played college football at Howard University, but that is not his main claim to fame. The 24-year-old running back had a significant impact during the UFL title game, rushing for 81 yards, and was named the game's MVP by the league. This past season, he played for the Louisville Knights in the UFL.

The Bills signed Wheeler right after the conclusion of the UFL season. And now he has a good chance of playing in the NFL this season, but maybe not in Buffalo.

Wheeler spent some time in the NFL before his current stint with the Bills. He signed a three-year, $2.8 million deal with the Chicago Bears as an undrafted free agent in 2024. But he never saw any significant playing time. He tore his ACL in the Bears' final preseason game that season, and the team waived him in August 2025.

Even though Wheeler has been out of the NFL for almost a year, he knows how lucky he is to have another opportunity.

"I saw this opportunity to compete on a very seasoned roster, on a roster that has had a lot of success these last few years," Wheeler said on Aug .19, via Bills.com's Mike Maynard. "It's definitely exciting to be granted the opportunity to be back in the league and nonetheless with a team like this."

It will be exciting to see how Wheeler ends his preseason when the Bills take on the Pittsburgh Steelers at Highmark Stadium on Thursday at 7 p.m ET.

title: Bears Projected to Cut Roschon Johnson in Favor of Ex-Dolphins RB
description: The latest 53-man roster projection for the Chicago Bears has them dumping one of their $4.6 million draft picks during the roster cutdown. The post Bears Projected to Cut Roschon Johnson in Favor of Ex-Dolphins RB appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears may soon reach the end of the road with former fourth-round running back Roschon Johnson as the 53-man roster cutdown draws nearer.

After several weeks of training-camp competition for the No. 3 running back role on the Bears' 2026 roster, ESPN's Courtney Cronin has projected that Johnson won't make the initial 53-man roster cut after playing in 36 games over the past three years in Chicago.

Cronin also predicted that former Miami Dolphins veteran Salvon Ahmed — who has stood out in the 2026 preseason — will take Johnson's place as the new No. 3 back.

"Swift had arguably the best training camp of any offensive skill player," Cronin wrote on August 24. "He and Monangai will continue to power a rushing attack that ranked third in 2025. Ahmed edges out former fourth-round pick Roschon Johnson for the role of RB3."

The Bears have a few different things to consider when deciding who will make the roster as their third-string running back in 2026. But if production on offense proves the most important element, then Ahmed has a distinct preseason lead over Johnson.

Through two preseason games, Ahmed has rushed for 53 yards on eight carries and logged multiple runs of 10-plus yards. He has also caught six passes for 69 receiving yards, including a screen pass from quarterback Case Keenum that he took 49 yards for a score in the 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns in the Bears' preseason opener.

Johnson received more carries than any other Bears running back in both the first (eight) and second preseason games (12), but he has averaged just 3.8 yards on those 20 combined carries. He also did little with his two receptions, netting just four yards.

At this point, Ahmed appears the frontrunner from an offensive production standpoint, more so than Johnson or Brittain Brown, who spent 2025 on Chicago's practice squad. That is not the only thing that will factor into the RB3 decision for the Bears, though.

Cronin's projection has Johnson on the outside looking in, but Bears head coach Ben Johnson cast doubt on that possibility in the postgame of their second preseason game.

Johnson ran for just 42 yards on 12 carries and caught a 1-yard reception on his only passing target during the Bears' 27-9 preseason loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, but that didn't stop his head coach from shouting out his recent improvement on special teams — the area that is likely to decide which player sticks around as their No. 3 running back.

"[Roschon Johnson] flashed the other day, in particular on special teams," Johnson said on August 22. "And we keep talking about the importance of being the No. 3 running back or depth in the running back room and being able to bring that to the table. He had a couple really nice plays in practice, can't wait to see what it looked like on game tape, because we talked about wanting to see players stack good performances back-to-back, and he's a candidate that may have done that tonight."

title: Hotter’N Hell Hundred celebrates 45 years of cycling, Roby Christie reflects
description: For more than four decades, thousands of cyclists have come to Wichita Falls ready to take on the heat and one hundred miles, but before Hotter 'N Hell Hundred became one of the city's most recognizable traditions, it was just an idea from one man.
fullText:
WICHITA FALLS (KFDX/KJTL) — For more than four decades, thousands of cyclists have come to Wichita Falls ready to take on the heat and one hundred miles, but before Hotter 'N Hell Hundred became one of the city's most recognizable traditions, it was just an idea from one man.

A wheel is meant to move the rider forward, but for Roby Christie, Hotter 'N Hell Hundred is a chance to look back

"Being there on day one means a lot to myself and my wife. We have been known to many as "father hotter" and "mother hell". So, just Hotter 'N Hell in general is ingrained in us. 45 Years of sharing our summers and long days during the year with the public," Christie said.

It started with an idea and a bicycle. Now, more than four decades later, and that idea is still rolling, bringing in thousands of cyclists to Wichita Falls and creating a legacy that its founders could have never imagined.

"The city of Wichita Falls with the chamber; they were preparing to celebrate the 100th birthday of Wichita Falls. I don't exactly know how I got chosen, but I was asked to come up with a kickoff event for the centennial," Christie said.

The city suggested holding a rocking chair marathon, but Christie had a different idea: a bike ride. Now, over 40 years later, that ride is recognized worldwide as one of the top bike marathons.

"It's humbling because we put a lot of work into it. We have a committee of 150 people or so. Our city and county put a lot of money and folks into it. To see that the potential riders in the United States and beyond have found value in that it is priceless to us," Christie said.

For Christie, his love for cycling came the day he got his first bike at five years old.

"I was given a bicycle by a neighborhood girl, and I rode that bicycle. The only thing wrong with that little bicycle was that there was a bolt on the frame, and every time my ankle would pass that I would get a bloody spot. Still, I rode that bike for a long time with bloody spots on my ankle, so I had to want to do it pretty bad," Christie said.

That first bike kicked his passion into gear and has connected him to thousands of people around the world who share a common interest.

"There are so many folks that have conquered illnesses, solves personal problems that they have in their lives by focusing on cycling, focusing on their health, and doing things that are good for them and others because they've seen so much good come out of the efforts of other people," Christie said.

Christie said if he could talk to his younger self, he'd tell him he's going to be a part of something really special, and it happened because so many people were involved.

For now, he's looking forward to the next big race.

title: Sharks Breakout Candidates: Michael Misa
description: Heading into his second year in the NHL, the San Jose Sharks would undoubtedly love to see Michael Misa take a massive step forward in his development.
fullText:
Heading into his second year in the NHL, the San Jose Sharks would undoubtedly love to see Michael Misa take a massive step forward in his development.

Misa, 19, had the disadvantage of great expectations heading into his rookie season. As the second-overall selection in the 2025 NHL Draft, it's easy to get caught by a whirlwind of expectations which can lead to disappointing performances. Luckily for Misa, the Sharks were no stranger to top prospects as they had Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith break into the NHL during the prior season.

Misa followed a similar plan to Smith's rookie season, as the Sharks allowed him to adjust to life in the NHL without wearing him out with the insane schedule that comes as a part of it. They'd sit him as needed, which allowed him to rest and learn by watching his teammates.

The Sharks likely would've preferred to see Misa on the ice more than 45 times last season, but injury, the World Junior Championships and some early contractual issues on the organization's side of things led to him being limited even more than expected.

Assuming Misa is able to stay healthy during his sophomore season, it seems safe to assume that the Sharks are going to aim to play him in all 84 games this time around. So, assuming he's able to do that, what would a successful season look like for the young centerman?

While offensive production is a key part of Misa's game, and it will be his biggest asset in the long run, the Sharks need to get him to a point where he can match up against other teams' top players if necessary. Misa will likely slot in as the Sharks' second-line center of the future, behind Celebrini of course. In the event that Celebrini suffers an injury at some point down the line, which the Sharks will need to be able to rely on Misa to cover all of his duties, which will include playing against the NHL's elite centers.

Misa will likely never be a candidate for the Selke Trophy, but they'll want him to be solid in his own zone and that side of his game needs a considerable amount of work at the NHL level. He was a reliable two-way player in the Ontario Hockey League, now he needs it to translate to the NHL.

On the offensive side of things, it's unrealistic to expect him to have a season like Celebrini did in his sophomore campaign. For Misa, a realistic target would likely be between 50-60 points in an 84 game season. Given his natural goal-scoring ability as well, roughly 20 of those should be goals.

All-in-all, the most important thing Misa needs to do for a successful season is to establish himself as the Sharks' second-line center as soon as possible. With the team aiming to push for a playoff spot this time around, Ryan Warsofsky and company will need Misa to surpass Alexander Wennberg for that spot. Even though Wennberg is a fantastic third-line center, he shouldn't be on the second line of a playoff team.

Expectations are undoubtedly going to be high for Michael Misa heading into his second NHL season, but that's nothing new for him. While there's always the possibility of a sophomore slump, he has all the tools to be a key player for the Sharks this season if he's able to put things together.

fullText:
SEATTLE (AP) — Seattle Mariners rookie shortstop Colt Emerson will have season-ending surgery on Wednesday to repair a partially dislocated tendon in his left wrist and is expected to be ready for the start of next season, general manager Justin Hollander said Monday.

Emerson has been bothered by the injury since before spring training.

The 21-year-old Emerson signed a $95 million, eight-year contract on April 1 — the biggest commitment at the time for a player who had yet to appear in the big leagues. In May, he became the youngest Mariners player to make his major league debut since Félix Hernández, who was 19 on Aug. 4, 2005.

He played well initially but struggled over the summer while battling the injury. He was hitting .190 with eight homers and 23 RBIs in 69 games when the Mariners announced earlier this month that they were optioning him to Triple-A Tacoma. The club said a day later that Emerson would instead be placed on the injured list.

Hollander said right-hander Bryan Woo would make his scheduled start on Wednesday.

Woo experienced shoulder soreness during his most recent start. Hollander said that Woo "felt something unusual" last week, but had not been able to reproduce it since and was feeling better after a bullpen session on Sunday.

"Bryan feels great," Hollander said. "No concerns on his part, he'll get out there on Wednesday and hopefully get after it."

Shortstop J.P. Crawford was expected to participate in warmups before Monday night's game against Philadelphia and was likely to be activated from the IL on Tuesday, Hollander said.

Infielder Brendan Donovan is still experiencing concussion symptoms after being hit in the head with a throw in the batting cage on Sunday. Hollander said Donovan will remain on the seven-day IL at least through the weekend.

The Detroit Lions' battle for the starting center position might have ended before it ever really started. Whether it be the words of Dan Campbell, the actions of the coaching staff in the preseason, or the reaction from the Lions' second preseason game, all indications point to Juice Scruggs being the Lions' starting center.

The team initially tried Seth McLaughlin at center, and he fared well. However, he started because Scruggs was out of the lineup. Once Scruggs returned, he was getting almost all of the first-team work.

When asked about the Lions starting center competition before the second preseason game, Campbell noted the experience Scruggs has at center as a key reason he will get the first chance. He noted Tate Ratledge sliding over in an emergency scenario before bringing up McLaughlin.

âThereâs a reason we got Juice in this trade,â Campbell told Brad Galli. âJuice has played in this league, and heâs played a lot of center snaps. Heâs played guard too, but center really, really suits him.â

In the second preseason game, Scruggs played 15 snaps, and McLaughlin played 52 snaps. However, starters Christian Mahogany, Blake Miller, Tate Ratledge, and even Larry Borom, who filled in for Penei Sewell, played 15 snaps.

Scruggs was given the starter treatment, while McLaughlin was given the treatment of a player who needs experience to prove he belongs in the NFL.

So far in the preseason, McLaughlin has 91 snaps and a 54.5 PFF grade. Meanwhile, Scruggs has 15 snaps and a 58.7 grade. He is being trusted more and performing better.

Anthony Balaj of Pride of Detroit did a film review of Scruggs, and after watching McLaughlin in comparison, his takeaway was clear. The team will be starting Scruggs.

"Juice Scruggs made his case on Saturday afternoon against the Washington Commanders in the Lionsâ second game of the 2026 preseason," wrote Balaj. "Despite some promising play from Seth McLaughlin in training camp, the competition may be over."

Nate Tice from Yahoo Sports largely agreed. He noted that if the Lions find ways to use him right, they will get the most out of him.

I thought Juice Scruggs (#70) had a nice showing in his first preseason action at Center for the Lions. Was sturdy and played with a good base in the run game & pass protection.

Like him better on Gap and Duo run concepts where he can use his size rather than on zone runs. pic.twitter.com/H2zQb4QXs8

— Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) August 24, 2026

"I thought Juice Scruggs (#70) had a nice showing in his first preseason action at Center for the Lions," tweeted Tice. "Was sturdy and played with a good base in the run game & pass protection. Like him better on Gap and Duo run concepts where he can use his size rather than on zone runs."

The Lions have been searching for a starter since their expected starter Cade Mays went down with a wrist injury that will extend into the 2026 regular season. The Lions acquired Scruggs from the Houston Texans along with a couple of draft picks for David Montgomery.

Montgomery looked like the big name in the deal, but if the Lions can walk away with draft capital and a replacement center for the time being, it is going to be viewed as a huge win for the team.

Scruggs has earned the starting job. Now he is going to have to continue to hold it down as McLaughlin progresses and Mays gets healthy.

title: Mariners Colt Emerson to have season-ending wrist surgery
description: A tough end to a tough debut season for the Mariners’ young shortstop
fullText:
Justin Hollander met with the media today to provide an update on Colt Emerson, the Mariners' young shortstop. Shortly after Emerson, who was hitting .190 at the time, was re-assigned to Triple-A, it was announced he'd instead go on the IL with a wrist injury that had been nagging at him in Tacoma but dated back to spring training. Emerson will have surgery on that wrist, performed by Dr. Donald Sheridan, an orthopedic hand and wrist surgeon, this Wednesday, ending his 2026 season.

The surgery will move a tendon in Emerson's wrist which has slipped out of place back to where it belongs, an injury known as a subluxation in the wrist. Warning: Gory Medical Details ahead. Skip to the next paragraph if this makes you squeamish. Most commonly in a wrist subluxation, the extensor carpi ulnaris (ECU) tendon, which runs along the outside of the pinky side of the hand, slips out of alignment – the "groove" on the bone it's located in. The most common symptom is a "popping" or "clicking" sound during movement, and in acute cases, swelling and inflammation. Since the ECU tendon is fundamental in actions like gripping and twisting, a severe injury clearly poses a problem for a professional baseball player.

It's a fairly common injury, and one that is often managed without surgery – J.P. Crawford has been dealing with a similar injury – depending on where the tendon is and what it's resting on. The soreness first popped up this spring in Arizona, and Emerson saw Dr. Sheridan at that time, whose diagnosis was that Emerson could elect to have surgery, but that he didn't have to have the surgery if he didn't want to. With a wide-open road to playing time with the incumbent shortstop Crawford dealing with a shoulder injury, and feeling like he could manage the occasional soreness, Emerson elected to continue to play.

"Different guys have different pain thresholds," said Hollander. "My belief is that Colt Emerson has a really high one, and he played to the point until he felt like it has crossed the threshold of being smart for him to continue." Hollander also says there are "no concerns" with Emerson being ready for next year.

It's hard to remember given how badly he slumped down the stretch, but Emerson got off to a strong start initially, hitting for average and power in May and June, with seven homers and five doubles. However, as his time in the big leagues wore on, pitchers found they could get Emerson to expand up out of the strikezone and chase the high fastball; by the time he was sent down in August he was striking out over 40% of the time.

It could be argued that a sore wrist was causing Emerson to be late on the fastball. His bat speed on Statcast is listed at 72 mph, which is about average, whereas his prospect numbers had him more around 75, classified as "fast" by Statcast. However, the sore wrist was likely a minor contributing factor in the biggest issue facing Emerson: his swing decisions. Never a free swinger in the minors, in the big leagues Emerson chased more than he ever had as a prospect, swinging 60% of the time in the Shadow zone (compared to MLB average 54%) and 34% of the time in the Chase zone (compared to MLB average 26%). He showed swing and miss vulnerabilities on all pitches, not just fastballs, whiffing 38% of the time on curveballs and 40% of the time on sliders.

As tough as Emerson's season was offensively, he also scuffled at times defensively, which could be related to the deteriorating pain in his wrist, especially as the ECU tendon plays such a role in gripping and twisting. Emerson was assessed eight errors at shortstop, six of them throwing errors.

The good news about all of this is there's nowhere to go but up for Seattle's young infielder, inked to an eight-year contract extension this year. Hopefully he'll follow in the footsteps of another young infielder for Seattle, Cole Young, who struggled in his debut but applied himself with specific energy this off-season and has been reaping the rewards of the off-season work he put in on both sides of the ball all season long. In a season that's not been very lucky for Emerson nor the Mariners, he's fortunate to have a role model to follow right in his own clubhouse.

One final note: As mentioned above, this is a similar injury to the one J.P. Crawford has been dealing with this season. Crawford, who has been rehabbing with Triple-A Tacoma, is with the team today and will probably be activated tomorrow depending on clearing pregame activities without incident, although Hollander called it "likely" he'd be activated.

title: Former Cincinnati Bearcats point guard Michael Horton dies
description: Former Cincinnati Bearcats point guard Michael Horton, who played two seasons for Bob Huggins, is dead.
fullText:
The Enquirer has confirmed that former University of Cincinnati Bearcats point guard Michael Horton has died.

An official cause of death is not available. Horton had just turned 50 in May.

Horton came to the Bearcats basketball as a junior college All-American from Allegany (Maryland) Community College and played his high school ball at T.C. Williams High School in Alexandria, Virginia, where he averaged 30 points and nine assists his senior season.

The 6-foot-1, 205-pound guard played on two UC teams that both went 27-6. They were Conference USA season champions both years and C-USA Tournament champions in 1998. Horton played with future NBA players Ruben Patterson and Kenyon Martin.

Martin mentioned Horton's passing on his Instagram account Aug. 24, writing: "Got some very Unfortunate news yesterday that my college teammate Michael Horton passed away! Sad day for our Bearcat family!!! Rest Easy Mike!!!!"

Former UC player and Bearcats broadcaster Terry Nelson spoke of Horton's passing and tenacity.

"Michael Horton was one of the best on-the-ball defenders we've had at UC in the past 25 years," Nelson said. "His toughness, his ability to fight through screens, really made him valuable as a point guard on our defense."

Horton started 26 of 29 games in 1997-98, averaging 6 points and 4.8 assists per game. He had a career-high 17 points in a C-USA quarterfinal tournament win over Louisville, with seven rebounds and seven assists. In the C-USA semifinal vs. UAB, he dished out 10 assists and made the all-tournament team.

He was injured the first month of his senior year, but returned in December, starting 14 of 24 games and averaging 3.6 points and 3.5 assists. He later had an ankle sprain but returned against Xavier in late January 1999 with 10 points and eight assists in an 87-77 win at then-Shoemaker Center.

Also on UC's team in Horton's final season were Shawn Myrick, Jermaine Tate, Alvin Mitchell, Melvin Levett, Steve Logan, Ryan Fletcher, Pete Mickeal, Eugene Land, Aaron McGhee, Donald Little and Alex Meacham. Meacham posted of his friendship with Horton on X.

RIP to my Bearcat teammate Michael Horton. I’ll never forget when Jay Z’s song “Imaginary Player” came on in the locker room and we went back and forth bar for bar every word of the song. Every time we saw each other, we would rap the lyrics and just laugh. Rest Easy Bearcat! 🙏🏼 pic.twitter.com/LOKRI0H0JS

The Bearcats were as high as No. 10 in the AP poll in 1997-98 and No. 11 in 1998-99 during Horton's time in Cincinnati

MIDLAND, Texas (KMID/KPEJ) -The Midland High Bulldogs are looking to turn the page in 2026 after a season that fell short of expectations.

Head coach Thad Fortune is entering his sixth season at Midland High and says the Bulldogs are approaching the new season with a renewed focus and appreciation for the opportunity to build the program.

"You have to come to work every day with a humble attitude that just trying to make this place the best I can while I get the opportunity to serve here," Fortune said. "So yeah, it's a huge honor to be in year six."

One of the biggest changes for Midland High this season is a new offensive system. After years of running the triple option, the Bulldogs are moving to a spread attack.

Fortune said making the switch has required plenty of work during the offseason, but the Bulldogs believe the new system fits their personnel.

"It's a long process and a lot to learn and a lot of ups and downs and good days and bad days and everything in the middle," Fortune said. "But we've, it's what we, it's a decision I made, you know, really probably Thanksgiving last year was when I really just decided that's what we were going to do."

Senior offensive lineman Jesus Garcia has embraced the change and believes the Bulldogs are buying into what their coaches are asking of them.

"It's something awesome. I mean, I got here when the coaches came, 21," Garcia said. "So I've been able to see the process, be able to buy in and just follow everything that they've expected from us."

Garcia is one of the senior leaders on a team looking to get back to the playoffs. He was part of Midland High's 2024 playoff team and wants to help the Bulldogs return to that level.

Ham also believes the team's chemistry can help them make that jump.

"We're all really good friends," Ham said. "Like our brotherhood was really good. It's, we all know each other. We're all friends and we hang out outside of football."

With a new offensive system, experienced senior leaders and plenty to prove, Midland High is hoping the changes lead to a different result in 2026.

title: NFL legend Ray Lewis brings more than photo op to Community School of Naples
description: NFL legend Ray Lewis visited Community School of Naples, speaking to high school and Pop Warner players about mental health for young athletes.
fullText:
Ray Lewis didn't know how to slow down.

He was wearing half pads, and his high school football coach had made it clear: There would be no tackling.

Then the play happened. Lewis hit the player anyway.

His coach couldn't believe it. He had just told the players there would be no tackling.

Lewis' response: "Coach, that wasn't even full speed."

"Don't change it. We'll change around you."

Decades later, that mentality still defines Lewis. It followed him from Lakeland Kathleen High School to the University of Miami and through 17 NFL seasons in Baltimore.

But the lesson Lewis took from that moment wasn't simply about playing hard. It was about having a coach who understood him.

Now, Lewis is trying to provide that same kind of influence for a new generation.

The Pro Football Hall of Famer spent part of Saturday, Aug. 22, at the Community School of Naples, talking with coaches, players and teachers before later addressing a smaller audience on campus during a Fellowship of Christian Athletes event.

"I'd do this the rest of my life for free," Lewis told USA TODAY Sports. "I want to see a young man that says, 'I get it.' A few of these kids came to me later (today) and said, 'I'm really struggling.' And they will never tell nobody else that. But you expose who you are. That's why I always give them my weaknesses. If you know my weaknesses, then you can appreciate my strengths.

"But if you don't know where I came from, then you're just gonna look at me as, 'Oh my gosh, you're Ray Lewis.' A lot comes with that. That's why I come to schools like this; it's a bonus. It's what I live my life with. Making the transition of losing my child, every time I take one of these boys' hands, I'm blessing somebody else."

Lewis shared plenty of stories about his past. His mother was 15 when she had him. He grew up without his biological father and watched his mother struggle to provide for him and his siblings.

Football wasn't initially an option because his family couldn't afford the $15 required to play. He went to practices anyway, sitting outside the gate and crying because he couldn't join the other players.

Then, in 1985, a coach approached him and asked why he wasn't playing. Lewis told him.

The coach went to his mother. After a three-hour conversation, Lewis got his chance.

That coach became one of the people Lewis still credits with changing his life. So did the coaches who followed.

Every coach Lewis had from high school and college remains in his phone. He still talks to them and sends them annual Father's Day messages. Three of them attended his Hall of Fame ceremony.

He didn't just listen to those coaches. He absorbed them.

He asked questions about drills and technique, often using the car rides home to understand why his coaches directed him to do something a certain way.

Looking back, Lewis believes his childhood circumstances made him more willing to learn from those men.

"I recognized them (at my Hall of Fame) because they gave me the leadership that my father wasn't around to give me," Lewis said. "... Every one of my coaches gave me that. All leadership, all fatherhood, all discipline, all responsibility, all integrity, all the character."

That experience shaped the way Lewis thinks about coaching. It's also part of why he has become so focused on what happens to young people away from the football field.

Lewis has partnered with Baltimore County Public Schools on a program focused on students' mental and emotional well-being. Launched in March, the pilot mental health screening program is set to enter its first full school year in Baltimore, with hopes of expanding the initiative statewide.

The work has taken on added meaning for Lewis following the loss of his eldest son in 2023, and he often speaks to kids about the importance of not being afraid to be vulnerable.

"You check their 40 (time), you check their hips," Lewis said. "You'll check their surgery history. But you won't check their minds."

He talked at CSN about how difficult it is for many young people to open up, particularly in a world where social media can make perception feel more important than reality. When young people know somebody genuinely cares about them, they're often willing to say things they have been holding inside.

CSN football player Benjamin Reseau was one of them.

Hearing Lewis' story didn't feel like listening to a distant NFL legend recount Reseau's childhood. The Seahawks senior saw parts of his own life in it.

Lewis talked about growing up without his father. Reseau lost his father to coronavirus during the pandemic. Lewis talked about his relationship with his mother, who he has described as his best friend. Reseau shares the same sentiment.

"I saw a connection in a lot of his characteristics and a lot of the things he's done over his life," Reseau said.

That connection made Lewis' message more personal.

Reseau previously struggled to open up about his own experiences, in part because he was afraid of being judged. Coming to CSN, where many students had grown up in circumstances far different from his own, made it difficult at times to explain what he had been through.

Over time though, he learned that keeping things inside wasn't helping. So when Lewis spoke, Reseau listened.

"I just thought today, something just told me to speak up," Reseau said. "I had to."

Lewis made sure to talk to Reseau after the discussion, and the two exchanged phone numbers.

"No one I've coached has handled so much adversity with grace," CSN football coach Jonah Dubinski said of Reseau.

For Dubinski, that was part of the challenge Lewis was addressing.

"We have kids on both extremes socioeconomically and culturally, and how do you reach those different kinds of kids with the same message?" Dubinski said. "And Ray's advice there was fantastic. Get away from results-driven analysis of performance and be process- and structure-oriented.

"That's dead on. You listen to (Nick) Saban, you listen to Ray Lewis, you listen to everyone who's done it at a high level. It's process-oriented."

That philosophy extends beyond football for Dubinski. CSN's goal is to develop young men and women first, trusting that the results on the field will follow. That's part of why having Lewis in the building carried more weight than simply showing the players a video or playing a motivational speech.

"A lot of what he said today, you can piece together from the hundreds of videos out there," Dubinski said. "But it impacted me differently. It certainly impacted the kids differently."

Two parts of Lewis' message particularly stuck with Reseau: hearing Lewis talk about losing his son and hearing him discuss the relationships he has maintained with his coaches.

Reseau said he already tries to maintain those relationships with his own coaches beyond football.

"I always try to make sure I'm connected with everybody on another level, like a relationship type," Reseau said. "Always try to leave a good footprint for myself, for everybody."

Lewis left the players with another piece of advice:

"Stop asking for the picture," he said. "Ask for knowledge."

title: Giants flip 19% of their roster; 3 to IL, 1 to bereavement, 1 optioned
description: Giants send their Tugboat back to AAA and place a trio on the IL. Meanwhile, Bryce Eldridge is on the bereavement list.
fullText:
It was too much to type for Giants beat writer Andrew Baggarly, but he helpfully copy-pasted the Giants' media release about their bevy of roster moves before tonight's kickoff against the Cincinnati Reds at Oracle Park:

That's 5 out of 26 players replaced in one fell swoop, which would be a big shock to the system if the Giants were expected to be competitive every night. Instead, it's a clear downgrade as minor league flotsam returns to replace questionably good major league talent.

Of course, first and foremost, condolences to Bryce Eldridge and his family. This would appear to be his maternal grandfather, as his paternal grandfather, bluegrass musician Ben Eldridge, passed away in 2024. While Eldridge is far away from the NL Rookie of the Year competition, it would've been fun to see him on the same field as potential winner Sal Stewart this series.

Meanwhile, Tugboat returns to Triple-A and would seem to be in line to return quickly when the next player winds up on the IL.

Willy Adames hurt himself in the 1st inning of Sunday's game and played through the 4th inning only to leave and be replaced by Buddy Kennedy. At the time, the team announced "an unspecified left elbow injury." Today, that was reported as a sprain.

As Alex Pavlovic commented yesterday:

For his part, he'd been having another typical Willy Adames second half and seemed set to approach his career totals. Since the All-Star break, he's slashed .231/.314/.435 (.749 OPS) over his last 30 games (121 PA). Not electric, but certainly evidence of timing and confidence back despite a tricky back issue. With this elbow sprain, his season seems just about wrapped up. .230/.289/.424 isn't what anyone hoped for (the Giants were also 48-73 in games played), but he still has 5 guaranteed years and $155.7 million coming his way, so, he'll be fine.

But it'll be a tough time for Victor Bericoto, who is going to miss some absolutely crucial development time. After yesterday's game, he said he was a little sore but in the moment "I thought I had damaged my knee really bad, because I felt pain really bad." A bone bruise isn't necessarily a season ender, but it's one of those tricky injuries that can linger and reaggravate.

The 24-year old already missed a good chunk of the season with an oblique strain and now this bone bruise threatens to eat up more time, just at the point when the team would've likely ran him out there every day to see where he fit into next year's plans. Now, a development delay and, later, a lockout that'll have him spinning his wheels and not getting better in his age-25 season. Tough. But, that's what happens to a rancid franchise with a hopeless future on the horizon.

JT Brubaker missing time with bruised ribs might be a godsend for the faithful Giants. Everyone on the broadcasting side wants to talk about his "nice season" as he's coughing up leads and generally being bad, but that's just what happens when a 3.58 ERA in 60.1 innings pitched takes precedence over a 4.26 FIP and 3.9 BB/9 versus a 5.8 K/9. He ought to be the last player on the roster. A virtual afterthought.

For someone with such a low leverage index (0.43 runs on the season — 1 or above is considered "high leverage"), his -0.291 Win Probability Added is pretty silly. And, since the All-Star break, he has a 6.08 ERA in 13.1 (11 appearances) or a 4.28 FIP. This would be addition by subtraction if not for the Giants' solution to these injuries:

Somehow, Ryan Walker has returned.

The human nuke is back to make Oracle Park and late innings for the Giants and their fans even more radioactive. His 7.52 ERA / 5.44 FIP on the season in no way merits another opportunity. Not for a 30-year old reliever. On the other hand… oof… a 1.63 ERA in Triple-A is pretty good. His 8.5 K/9 also pretty good. 2.9 BB/9 also good. And, again, it's not like the Giants are playing for anything… maybe these next 4 weeks can be an audition for some team to take him in the offseason. Who knows?

Speaking of offseason moves, while the Giants seem like to release him at season's end, their return for Tyler Mahle, Anthony Molina, is up. He struck out 9 and walked 2 in 9 IP for the River Cats. That'll work. Worth seeing what he's got for a fourth stint in the big leagues.

As for infielder Shay Whitcomb, the Giants claimed the 27-year old off waivers from the Astros a week and a half ago. This is one of those players where the hand of Zack Minasian feels particularly present. He was the pro scout for the Brewers and so seeing a 6-year minor leaguer with an .810 OPS is what he lived and breathed for a good chunk of time. Whitcomb had just a .669 OPS in 35 River Cats PAs, but with Adames down, needing someone who could handle shortstop a little bit has become important. He has over 2,000 MiLB innings at the position.

Nate Furman and Grant McCray both provide left-handed warm bodies for the Giants' lineup AI and so I am not sure we're meant to expect anything more than that from this pair.

title: How a human trafficking sting in a tiny Ohio town snared 49ers owner | Exclusive
description: Mayor Trent Conaway reacted to Jed York's arrest by saying his town hadn't had as much excitement since a 2023 train derailment brought national attention.
fullText:
Trent Conaway works a full-time job as a logistics coordinator for a trucking company. His other job, mayor of the village of East Palestine, Ohio, is a part-time gig.

"We haven't had this much excitement around here since the train derailed," Conaway told USA TODAY Sports by phone Aug. 24. "It's been a little chaotic the last couple of hours, but yeah."

Conaway, who spoke at the 2024 Republican National Convention, was referencing two events more than three years apart. The train derailment near the small town of approximately 5,000 residents in northeast Ohio exposed the area to toxic chemicals during a lengthy cleanup process.

The "last couple of hours" was the arrest of San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York during a prostitution sting. York pleaded no contest Monday to two misdemeanor charges after his arrest in East Palestine, Ohio, on Aug. 23. York's initial charge of "engaging in prostitution" was reduced to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools, according to court documents obtained by USA TODAY Sports.

Policing human trafficking has been a priority in the area, Conaway said. Local detective Daniel A. Haueter works with the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, which is led by the Mahoning County Sheriff's Office and includes representatives from several agencies in the region, including the East Palestine Police Department.

Ohio Attorney General Dave Yost announced in May that more than 1,000 arrests had been made in human trafficking operations in the state since 2019, noting 10 arrests made by the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force in a coordinated statewide operation that month.

From what Conaway learned this was a normal prostitution sting conducted to root out human trafficking in the area.

"It just so happens," he said, "we got Mr. York."

The operations have been ongoing for about a decade, Conaway said, although he could not pinpoint exactly when they began.

Asked if human trafficking is a prevalent issue in the area, Conaway said it was a statewide effort to eliminate human trafficking and again complimented Haueter.

"We're very proud of the work that he's done. We've got quite a few people off the streets," Conaway said.

Conaway said those arrested for sex work are often directed to county- and state-level resources upon release from custody.

Catching the perpetrators seeking to pay for sex is the priority, though.

"We get people from all walks of life. It's a shame when anybody feels a need to do this. It doesn't matter whether they're a NFL owner or a handyman down the street," Conaway said. "We're trying to curb this. It's part of a broader scope of the human trafficking (enforcement). Human trafficking is a real problem. It's an ever-growing problem in the United States. We're just trying to do our best to curb that."

Contributing: Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz

title: Blazers star Shaedon Sharpe facing lengthy absence after major knee injury
description: The Trail Blazers were dealt a major offseason blow after Shaedon Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus that could sideline the rising star for six months.
fullText:
Blazers star Shaedon Sharpe facing lengthy absence after major knee injury originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Portland Trail Blazers will open the 2026-27 season without one of their top young scorers.

Guard Shaedon Sharpe sustained a torn meniscus in his right knee during a recent offseason workout and is expected to miss approximately six months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

The timeline puts a significant portion of Sharpe's upcoming season in jeopardy and represents another frustrating injury setback for the 23-year-old as Portland prepares to take another step forward.

Sharpe averaged 20.8 points per game last season, establishing himself as one of Portland's primary offensive weapons. However, his breakout campaign was interrupted when a stress fracture in his left fibula forced him to miss a substantial stretch.

Now, Sharpe faces another lengthy rehabilitation process, this time involving his right knee.

The timing is particularly difficult because Sharpe is entering the first season of the four-year, $90 million extension he signed with Portland last year. He is scheduled to earn approximately $20 million during the 2026-27 season.

Portland, however, is better positioned than most teams to absorb the loss in its backcourt.

The Trail Blazers are set to enter the season with veterans Ja Morant, Damian Lillard and Jrue Holiday on the roster. Their presence gives Portland considerable experience and flexibility while Sharpe recovers.

Lillard provides shooting and playmaking, Morant brings explosive scoring and pressure at the rim, and Holiday gives Portland a proven two-way option capable of defending multiple positions.

Still, replacing Sharpe's athleticism and scoring production will not be simple.

The former No. 7 overall pick has developed into an important part of Portland's long-term plans, with his ability to attack the basket and create his own shot making him a potentially dangerous complement to the team's veteran guards.

If Sharpe's six-month recovery timetable holds, his absence could extend well into the regular season.

For Portland, the immediate focus will be navigating the opening months without him.

For Sharpe, the challenge becomes another rehabilitation — and another attempt to return healthy enough to resume his rise as one of the Trail Blazers' most important young pieces.

title: Memphis adding former Miami coach Randy Shannon to Charles Huff staff
description: Days before its season-opening game on the road against UNLV, Memphis coach Charles Huff is adding major firepower to his Tigers staff
fullText:
Days before his team opens its 2026 season, Memphis coach Charles Huff is making a significant hire to his coaching staff.

Two people with direct knowledge of the situation tell USA TODAY Sports that Huff is adding former Miami Hurricanes head coach Randy Shannon as an senior defensive analyst and assistant to the head coach.

Memphis opens the Huff era Saturday on the road in Week 0 at UNLV -- the first of two demanding, early-season non-conference games against fellow Group of Six foes with potential College Football Playoff aspirations. The Tigers play at Boise State in Week 3.

Most recently, Shannon served on the Florida State coaching staff of Mike Norvell. With the Seminoles, Shannon held multiple defensive roles -- including defensive coordinator. His last season at Florida State was 2024.

As a player, Shannon won national titles with Miami as both a player and assistant coach; he garnered the Broyles Award in 2001 as college football's top assistant coach.

Shannon posted an 28-22 mark as Hurricanes head coach and later was 1-3 as interim head coach at Florida in 2017 when the Gators parted ways with former coach Jim McElwain.

Huff has quickly ascended the coaching ranks since first becoming a head coach at Marshall prior to the 2021 season.

He won 32 games in four years at Marshall, a run that included an upset on the road at Notre Dame and concluded with the program's 2024 Sun Belt Conference Championship.

That crown marked the Thundering Herd's first-ever SBC title.

He was hired away by Southern Mississippi and went 7-6, delivering just the second bowl berth this decade for the Golden Eagles.

When Ryan Silverfield was hired by Arkansas this offseason, Huff quickly was lured away by Memphis.

title: Jake Bennett’s workload may finally be catching up to the Red Sox rookie phenom
description: Bennett was a workhorse for Boston, and now that workload is starting to wear him down.
fullText:
Jake Bennett's workload may finally be catching up to the Red Sox rookie phenom originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

While the Boston Red Sox were able to complete the sweep yesterday against the San Francisco Giants, their starting pitcher Jake Bennett was lit up in the first couple of innings, giving up three runs before Boston had a chance to score.

When he was first called up, Bennett was a phenom for the Red Sox. However, in his past few, it's looking like the innings he's pitched are catching up to him.

Through his first 10 starts, Bennett looked perfect. He was 5-3 with a 2.58 ERA, 42 strikeouts, and a 0.940 WHIP in 59.1 innings pitched.

With his hot start, it looked like Boston absolutely won the trade for him with the Washington Nationals. Although, now it seems like something is wrong with their rising star in his recent starts.

Bennett has been getting blown up in his past five starts, and it seems the greatness he had in the first 10 starts is losing its luster.

In his last 10 starts, Bennett has posted a 2-3 record, a 5.40 ERA, 25 Ks, and a WHIP of 1.340 over 28 innings pitched.

To be fair to him, it's not really his fault, as he's just hit his current limit. He's dozens of innings over his career-high before this season, and he had Tommy John surgery just a couple years ago.

The big question is, can he recover before October? While they won't need him in the Wild Card round, they will need him if they make it to the ALDS.

Most likely, he'll be fine. Looking at yesterday's start, while he did give up three runs early, he got better and better as the game went on.

In his first time through the order, Bennett gave up four hits, a walk, a homer, and three runs. His second time, he gave up two hits. His third, one. He then got two outs in his fourth, and then was pulled out of the game.

Bennett still has it, it's just he's getting a little tired. Hopefully, he can right the course before the playoffs, and become the phenom Boston knows him to be once more.

title: Alabama Investigates OpenAI on HuggingFace Hacking Incident
description: Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall launched an investigation into OpenAI’s security procedures after one of its AI agents escaped a testing environment and hacked AI firm Hugging Face in July.
fullText:
Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall launched an investigation into OpenAI’s security procedures after one of its AI agents escaped a testing environment and hacked AI firm Hugging Face in July.

OpenAI now faces a subpoena to hand over information about all employees involved in the model testing leading up to the July incident, during which an OpenAI agent powered by the companies’ frontier AI models accessed the internet and several computer networks, and attacked Hugging Face.

“This AI lab leak showed that Alabamians’ and Americans’ worst fears about artificial intelligence are not just theoretical. Our investigation seeks to uncover the facts and address hard truths about the threats companies and consumers are facing from rogue AI,” Marshall said.

The subpoena, made public Monday, follows a letter sent earlier this month by a coalition of a dozen attorneys general that asked OpenAI to preserve relevant documentation about the security incident and halt all further similar testing of its models.

OpenAI is “conducting a thorough review along with external advisors,” a company spokesperson said. “Once the review is complete, we will share a technical report with relevant government authorities and publish our findings publicly.”

The company has been directed to hand over information about all networks, websites, and databases involved in the security incident, as well as information about safety measures it put in place during model testing. The AI giant has also been told to name every OpenAI employee, officer, and agent who raised concerns relating to the security of any model testing.

title: Poka-Yoke: Mistake-Proofing Claude Code Skill for Software
description: Mistake-proofing for software. Shigeo Shingo's poka-yoke method as a Claude Code plugin: audit code for footguns, design APIs that resist misuse, install guardrails, turn incidents into devices...
fullText:
An agent will tell you what to fix. It will rarely tell you what its fix makes impossible.

Unprompted, models close a design by naming what it forecloses 42% of the time. With
these skills, 81%, measured across 80 graded verdicts and six model families. That one
habit is most of what this does, and it is the difference between advice you agree with and
a constraint you can rely on.

A dependency-free hazard scanner for TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust and SQL; installable
pre-commit / CI / lint / hook devices; and 11 skills that apply the same method while
you design. Shigeo Shingo's method, applied to
code, process, interfaces, infrastructure, and AI.

Runs on 19 agent runtimes from one set of skills, 10 with a native manifest.
Benchmarked on Claude Code;
the support tiers are stated honestly.

591 blind-graded runs across six runtimes, at the first turn of a fresh session, scored
against pre-written assertions by a grader that never sees which configuration produced a
response. Every model improves on a no-skill baseline by more than noise: Fable 5
+8.3 pp, Opus 5 +3.6 pp, Sonnet 5 +8.6 pp, Haiku 4.5 +12.9 pp: all four 95%
intervals exclude zero. Nine of the 52 cells came out negative, where chance alone would
produce about 18: individual cells hold 1 to 7 runs and are too small to read on their own,
so the scarcity of regressions is the signal rather than their existence.
See the numbers.

All 591 runs are verified against the scenario prompts as they stand in this commit.

What this does not yet establish. Blind grading controls bias, not accuracy. The baseline
is no skill, not a different methodology, so whether any structured method in context
would do the same is untested; a control arm is designed and unrun. And every run is a first
turn, which measures the ceiling rather than what survives an afternoon of accumulated
context. The full list of what the numbers cannot tell you.

Loading a method changes what a model attends to, and attention is finite. Measured across the
same 591 runs, the skills make responses markedly more constructive and slightly worse at
noticing the specific defect already in front of them:

So: if you want the bug in front of you found, use a reviewer. If you want the shape changed
so that class of bug stops being expressible, use this. Loading it for the first job makes
the model measurably worse at it. That trade is the product, not a caveat about it.

People will always make mistakes. That is not the problem worth solving: the problem is
letting a mistake become a defect.

Shigeo Shingo: the industrial engineer who named poka-yoke and worked it out on the factory
floor, built his quality method on that distinction. Instead of asking workers to be more
careful, he redesigned the work so a mistake could not survive it. Assemblers kept forgetting
a spring inside a switch, so he had them lay both springs in a dish first: a spring still in
the dish was the error announcing itself, before the unit could move on.

This plugin applies that method to software. Not as a metaphor: the taxonomy is the actual
working tool. Every finding is classified by what happens when the mistake occurs and
how the device notices, which is what keeps it from collapsing into generic code review.

The line that does most of the work:

A comment, a docstring, a wiki page, a review checklist, or a line in CLAUDE.md saying
"don't do X" is not a poka-yoke. It is training, and training degrades. A device does
not. If your fix relies on someone remembering something, keep going.

You have already tried writing the rule down. Every repository that needs this has a
CLAUDE.md, an AGENTS.md or a CONTRIBUTING.md with a list of things everyone is supposed to
remember, and the list is longer than it was a year ago because the reminders did not hold. That
list is the real alternative to this plugin, not an unassisted model, and the argument here is
about why it decays and what to put in its place.

That is also the honest limit of the current evidence: the benchmark compares skill against
no skill, which is not the comparison you face. The comparison you face is against the rules
file you already wrote, and it has not been run yet.

Or just ask for it by name, "poka-yoke this repo", "mistake-proof this API", "run a
poka-yoke audit on src/billing". Both work.

What does not currently work is Claude reaching for these unprompted from a plain
description of a problem. That's measured, not assumed, see
invocation.

~/.claude/skills/ to commit it for the whole team. The second cp lands beside skills/,
